name: pm_pms5003
title: Dust sensor
purpose: Connector for a Plantower PMS5003 particle sensor (cabled, off the board): 5 V, UART, sleep and reset

sources.title: Plantower PMS5003 datasheet PTQ3004-2015 V1.0 (2019-7-31)
sources.licence: copyright Plantower: link and quotes only
sources.read: section 6 pin definition, section 8 circuit attentions, specifications (current, interface level)

sources.title: John Romkey, "Found: Plantower PMS3003, PMS5003, PMS7003 connectors" (blog, 2018)
sources.read: the connector part number (not a maker document)

sources.title: Raspberry Pi RP2040 datasheet
sources.licence: CC BY-ND 4.0: link and quotes only
sources.read: GPIO function table (UART0 TX/RX on GPIO12/13)

sources.title: KiCad 10 standard libraries (symbols, footprints, 3D models)
sources.read: symbol pin numbers, footprint pads, 3D models

parts.source: pms5003, section 6 (pins); romkey (connector part); kicad (footprint, 3D model)
parts.quote: romkey: "The cable needs a Molex 053261-0871 female connector, which has a 1.25mm pitch 'PicoBlade' header."; pms5003: "PIN1 VCC Positive power 5V; PIN2 GND ... PIN3 SET ... PIN4 RXD ... PIN5 TXD ... PIN6 RESET ... PIN7 NC; PIN8 NC"

VBUS.note: "DC 5V power supply is needed because the FAN should be driven by 5V"; active current ≤100 mA (pms5003)

/PM_RXD.note: the sensor's receive pin: to the RP2040's UART0 TX (GPIO12, rp2040 function table); "TTL level@3.3V"

/PM_TXD.note: the sensor's send pin: to UART0 RX (GPIO13)

/PM_SET.note: "high level or suspending is normal working status, while low level is sleeping mode"; pulled up inside the sensor

/PM_RESET.note: "low reset"; pulled up inside the sensor

layout.rules: "The SET and RESET pins are pulled up inside so they should not be connected if without usage." "PIN7 and PIN8 should not be connected." (pms5003 section 8)

open_questions: The connector part comes from a blog post, not a Plantower or Molex document: check the cable before ordering boards.
Pin 1 is at the left end of the sensor's connector in the datasheet's photo (Figure 2); the cable is assumed straight through (pin 1 to pin 1).
